meta.note: Copy for the interactive architecture on how.html. Editing this file changes the site; no JavaScript changes are needed.

frame.label: Frame
frame.question: What decision needs evidence?
frame.summary: A decision need is stated with its threshold, then decomposed into common questions that can each be answered separately.

assess.label: Assess
assess.question: Can this source answer this question?
assess.summary: Characterisation reports what a source actually contains. Fitness is then judged for a question × source pair, never for a database in general.

implement.label: Implement
implement.question: What travels to each site?
implement.summary: The coordinating centre sends one artefact per architecture: a question, a protocol, or an analytic program. Person-level data never leave the site.

interpret.label: Interpret
interpret.question: Do the results hold together?
interpret.summary: Aggregate outputs are pooled with a consistency check, examined through diagnostics, and tested for whether they inform another population.

integrate.label: Integrate
integrate.question: Is the totality enough to decide?
integrate.summary: Evidence is integrated across questions and judged against the threshold defined at the start. What falls short defines the next round.

decision-need.label: Decision need
decision-need.summary: The clinical, regulatory, or policy decision that the evidence has to support. The threshold for what would count as sufficient is set here, before any data are examined.

common-questions.label: Common questions
common-questions.summary: The decision need is decomposed into separately answerable questions, so that a source unfit for one facet can still contribute to another.

disease-burden.label: Disease burden
disease-burden.summary: How much unmet need exists, and in whom. Prevalence and incidence questions are usually the least demanding of a data source.
disease-burden.case: CASE 02 · AD / PN — prevalence measured under three case definitions of increasing specificity.

link.text: See the AD / PN prevalence work

treatment-use.label: Treatment use
treatment-use.summary: Which treatments are given, to whom, and in what sequence. Answering this requires dispensing or prescribing records with usable dates.
treatment-use.case: CASE 02 · AD / PN — index medication profiles compared across data environments.

effectiveness.label: Effectiveness
effectiveness.summary: Whether a treatment or a risk classification distinguishes outcomes. This is the most demanding facet: it needs exposure, outcome, covariates, follow-up, and a defensible time zero.
effectiveness.case: CASE 01 · ASCVD — whether a guideline-based stratification continued to distinguish recurrent risk.

safety.label: Safety
safety.summary: Long-term or rare adverse outcomes. Often the facet that most needs several data environments, because single sources rarely carry enough events.

link.text: When a question needs more than one source

data-characterisation.label: Data characterisation
data-characterisation.summary: Counts, coverage, coding availability, and temporal completeness are examined before any analysis is specified. This is descriptive work, and it is a deliverable in its own right.

characterisation-plots.label: Characterisation plots
characterisation-plots.summary: The descriptive output of characterisation: cohort assembly, baseline composition, and distributions, reviewed before anyone reads an effect estimate.

fit-for-purpose.label: Fit-for-purpose assessment
fit-for-purpose.summary: Fitness is a property of a question × source pair, not of a database. The same environment can be fit for a burden question and unfit for an effectiveness question.

coordinating-centre.label: Coordinating centre
coordinating-centre.summary: Sends one artefact to every participating site and receives only permitted aggregate output in return. It never receives person-level data.

common-question.label: Common question
common-question.summary: Only the research question travels. Each site chooses its own design, definitions, and methods, so local flexibility is highest and implementation variation is highest too.

common-protocol.label: Common protocol
common-protocol.summary: Design, eligibility, variable definitions, and analytic methods travel. Each site builds its own local implementation of that protocol.

common-data-model.label: Common data model
common-data-model.summary: Native data are conformed to a shared structure so one analytic program can run everywhere. The lowest implementation variation, at the cost of mapping and infrastructure work.
common-data-model.case: CASE 01 · ASCVD — this case exercised the common-data-model pathway across East Asian environments.

pooling.label: Pooling and assessing consistency
pooling.summary: Aggregate results are brought together and checked for consistency across sites and designs. Displaying a range is not the same as pooling an estimate.

diagnostics.label: Visualisation and diagnostics
diagnostics.summary: Balance, overlap, and negative controls are inspected before an estimate is interpreted. Diagnostics are how implementation problems are separated from real differences.

transportability.label: Assessing transportability
transportability.summary: Whether an estimate from one study sample can inform a different target population, while preserving the differences between them rather than averaging them away.
transportability.case: CASE 03 · TRANSPORTABILITY — estimates from Taiwan examined against a Japanese setting.

second-best.label: Second-best analysis
second-best.summary: Where a question × database pair fails the assessment, execution is bypassed. The questions are redefined, data partners extended, or a prospective or external control used — and the cycle returns to step 1.

evidence-integration.label: Evidence integration and visualization
evidence-integration.summary: Findings across questions are assembled into a totality, with each contribution weighted by the design that produced it and the context it came from.

fit-for-decision.label: Fit-for-decision
fit-for-decision.summary: To what extent do the findings inform the decision? The totality is compared with the threshold set in step 1. Whatever falls short defines the next round.

next-iteration.label: Next iteration
next-iteration.summary: The common layers are rebuilt with what was learned: a re-scoped question, extended mappings, additional sites, or an alternative design. Preparedness is iterative, not one-off.

results.label: Results
results.summary: Each site returns permitted aggregate output to the coordinating centre. Person-level data never leave the approved local environment.

intro.title: Nine steps from decision need to decision
intro.body: Every numbered step is explained here. Select any box in the diagram to see what it means, which case exercised it, and where its technical detail lives.
